{{Short description|Research collective}}
The '''Kraków School of Mathematics''' ({{langx|pl|krakowska szkoła matematyczna}}) was a subgroup of the [[Polish School of Mathematics]] represented by mathematicians from the [[Kraków]] universities—[[Jagiellonian University]], and the Mining Academy (now [[AGH University of Science and Technology|AGH University of Krakow]])–active during the [[interwar period]] (1918–1939). Their areas of study were primarily [[classical analysis]], [[differential equation]]s, and [[analytic function]]s.

The Kraków School of Differential Equations was founded by [[Tadeusz Ważewski]], a student of [[Stanisław Zaremba (mathematician)|Stanisław Zaremba]], and was internationally appreciated after [[World War II]]. 

The Kraków School of Analytic Functions was founded by [[Franciszek Leja]]. Other notable members included [[Kazimierz Żorawski]], [[Władysław Ślebodziński]], [[Stanisław Gołąb]], and [[Czesław Olech]].
